objectives: Học và thực hành: Passive voice (present/past simple passive; passive with by).

Đọc và hiểu đoạn Kinh Thánh Isaiah 53; Isaiah 55.

vocabulary.ex: Isaiah was a prophet who spoke God's word to Israel.
Isaiah's prophecy about the Servant came true in Jesus.
The Lord calls Jesus His Servant in Isaiah 53.
He was wounded for our transgressions.

vocabulary.vi: Sự vi phạm, sự phạm tội
vocabulary.ex: Our transgressions separated us from God.

vocabulary.vi: Bị nghiền nát, bị đè bẹp
vocabulary.ex: He was crushed for our iniquities.
The Lord laid on Him the iniquity of us all.
He was pierced for our transgressions.

vocabulary.vi: Bị khinh bỉ, bị khinh thường
vocabulary.ex: He was despised and rejected by men.

vocabulary.vi: Bị chối bỏ, bị từ bỏ
vocabulary.ex: Many people rejected the Servant, but God accepted Him.
The Servant knew suffering and grief.
He carried our sorrows and our grief.
He was a man of sorrows, acquainted with grief.
Jesus carried the burden of our sins.
God invites everyone: Come, all you who are thirsty.
Come, all you who are thirsty, come to the waters.
Seek the Lord while He may be found.
Let the wicked forsake his way.
God will have mercy on all who return to Him.
He will abundantly pardon.
God will abundantly pardon those who turn to Him.
God restores all who come to Him in faith.

reading_comprehension.q: 1. When did Isaiah live, and who was he?
reading_comprehension.a: About 700 years before Jesus; a prophet who spoke God's word to Israel.

reading_comprehension.q: 2. What did the Servant suffer, according to Isaiah 53:5?
reading_comprehension.a: He was wounded for our transgressions and crushed for our iniquities.

reading_comprehension.q: 3. What does 'by His wounds we are healed' mean?
reading_comprehension.a: Because Jesus suffered in our place, we can be forgiven and have peace with God.

reading_comprehension.q: 4. How is God's invitation in Isaiah 55 different from buying something in a shop?
reading_comprehension.a: It is completely free — no money, no cost; forgiveness is given by grace.

listening_questions.q: 1. How many years before Jesus was Isaiah a prophet?
listening_questions.a: About 700 years before Jesus was born.

listening_questions.q: 2. True or False: Isaiah 53 was written after Jesus came.
listening_questions.a: False — it was written long before Jesus came.

listening_questions.q: 3. According to Isaiah 53, why was the Servant wounded and crushed?
listening_questions.a: For our transgressions and our iniquities — He took our place.

listening_questions.q: 4. According to Isaiah 55, what does God invite thirsty people to do, and what does it cost?
listening_questions.a: To come to the waters (come to God); it is free — without money and without cost.

listening_questions.q: 5. What does Isaiah 55 say we should do, and what will God do in return?
listening_questions.a: Seek the Lord, call on Him, forsake our wicked ways and return to Him; He will have mercy and freely pardon.

exercises.title: Exercise 1: Weak Forms — Strong or Weak?
exercises.instruction: In natural speech the words of, to, and, have are usually WEAK (short, with /ə/). Underline the weak word in each sentence and write its weak pronunciation.

exercises.title: Exercise 2: Make the Passive
exercises.instruction: Complete each sentence with the correct passive form: is / are / was / were + past participle.

exercises.title: Exercise 3: Active to Passive
exercises.instruction: Rewrite each sentence in the passive. Keep the same tense.

exercises.title: Exercise 4: Vocabulary Matching
exercises.instruction: Match each word with its correct definition.

exercises.title: Exercise 5: Reading — True or False?
exercises.instruction: Read the passage in Section 5 again. Mark T (true) or F (false). Correct the false sentences.

exercises.title: Exercise 6: Translation Lab (Vietnamese to English)
exercises.instruction: Translate into natural English. Use the passive voice where the Vietnamese sentence focuses on the person who receives the action.

speaking_task: Roleplay in pairs (3 minutes): Student A invites Student B to church using Isaiah 55:1 ('Come, all you who are thirsty...'). Student B asks two questions. Use at least 3 passive sentences (e.g. 'You are invited...', 'Forgiveness is given freely...', 'We are welcomed by God...') and 4 vocabulary words from Section 3.
writing_task: Write an invitation message (80-100 words) to a friend who is far from God, based on Isaiah 55:1-7. Use at least 3 passive sentences and 4 vocabulary words from Section 3. Begin: 'Dear friend, I want to share some wonderful news with you...'

written: A. Rewrite these 5 active sentences in the passive: 1) God called Isaiah to be a prophet. 2) The soldiers pierced Jesus on the cross. 3) People rejected the Servant. 4) God offers living water to the thirsty. 5) The Lord forgives all who return to Him.
B. Write 6 sentences about Isaiah 53 using the passive voice (use: wounded, crushed, despised, rejected, pierced, laid).
homework.listening: Listen to the audio again. Fill in the missing words: 'He was ______ for our transgressions. He was ______ for our iniquities. The punishment that brought us ______ was on him, and by his ______ we are healed.' Then answer: What did the Friend decide to do this week?
homework.memory_verse: He was pierced for our transgressions; He was crushed for our iniquities; upon Him was the chastisement that brought us peace, and with His wounds we are healed. — Isaiah 53:5 (ESV). Also learn Isaiah 55:1: Come, everyone who thirsts, come to the waters.
